title: Bug Hunt: Fuzzing & Exploit Pipeline
story:
[BUG HUNTING MISSION - PART 3]
In real bug bounty hunting, directory fuzzers emit hundreds of timeout errors on `stderr` and HTTP status results on `stdout`. Once you filter and sort the live `200 OK` endpoints using pipes, you replay SQL injection payloads (`~/recon/payloads.txt`) into a vulnerable login tester (`/challenge/sqli_runner`) and capture the database debug dump on `stderr`.
objective:
Using ONLY taught commands (`2>/dev/null`, `|`, `grep`, `sort`, `>`, `<`, `2>`, `cat`):
1. Stage 1 (Fuzzer Triage): Run `/challenge/dirfuzz`, silence `stderr` (`2>/dev/null`), pipe `stdout` through `grep "200 OK"` and `sort`, and save the result to `~/recon/live_endpoints.txt`.
2. Stage 2 (SQLi Replay): Feed `~/recon/payloads.txt` into `/challenge/sqli_runner` via `<` (or `|`) while redirecting its `stderr` database error dump to `~/recon/db_error.log` (`2> ~/recon/db_error.log`).
3. Read `~/recon/db_error.log` (or run `quest check`) to get your `CYBERUS{...}` flag and submit it!
hints: Verify `cat ~/recon/live_endpoints.txt` shows only sorted `[200 OK]` lines and no errors or `404` lines.
Stage 2 command: `/challenge/sqli_runner < ~/recon/payloads.txt 2> ~/recon/db_error.log > /dev/null`, then run `grep "CYBERUS" ~/recon/db_error.log` or `quest check`.
